No, that is not correct. In Switzerland, the basic insurance (obligatory health insurance) includes an annual **franchise** and a **co-payment**.

- The **franchise** is the amount you must pay yourself each year before your insurance starts covering medical costs. For adults, the standard franchise is **CHF 300 per year** (you can choose a higher franchise, up to CHF 2,500, which reduces your monthly premium). There is **no unlimited co-payment** after the franchise: after you have paid the franchise, you also pay **10 % of the additional costs (up to a maximum of CHF 700 per year)** and a small additional charge (CHF 10 per day for hospital stays).

So, to summarize:
- Standard adult franchise: **CHF 300** per year (not CHF 150).
- There is a **maximum co-payment** (CHF 700 per year plus CHF 10 per day in hospital).

If you selected a higher franchise (e.g., CHF 500 or CHF 2,500), your monthly premium will be lower, but the co-payment cap still applies.
